decision.about: The brief says "the band head's line reads conclusions first" — asks.js has two things called a head: the whole wall's own head (`summary()`, `.ai-asks-head`, printed once) and each topic's own band heading (`heading()`, `.ai-asks-topic`, printed once per band).

options.say: Add it once, to the wall's own head line
options.why: The brief's own singular wording ("the band head's line", not "each band's") and the cap of one short label fit one line printed once, not five repeats of the same three words on every topic.

options.say: Add it to every topic band's heading
options.why: "Band" is the word this codebase uses for a topic group, so a literal reading points at `heading()`, repeated per band.

decision.because: One line, once, at the top of the tab says what kind of report this is without repeating itself five times down the page — and the wall's own head is the only "head" that is singular by construction.

decision.about: How does `ask.minutes` render beside the status chip?

options.say: A plain `.muted` span, no new class
options.why: Most cards never show it — the owner's own words, "most items should read in under a minute" — so it should read as a quiet aside, not a colored pill competing with the status chip for attention. Zero new CSS.
Visually matches the existing `needs you · N min` chip pattern (`.ai-ask-needs`) and stands out at a glance.

decision.because: The needs-you chip earns its color because it blocks a thread; an effort estimate is background information for the rare item that needs one, and a second colored pill next to `status` would out-shout it. Reuses the `.muted` utility already in this file's own foot row.

decision.about: Does the sheet's new "you asked" block show for every ask, or only ones carrying a conclusion?

options.why: The brief ties the move explicitly to the conclusion taking the title's place; an ask with no conclusion still shows its summary right on the card (unchanged, per deliverable 1), so repeating it in the sheet too would be the same sentence twice on one screen.

options.say: Show it on every ask's sheet, conclusion or not
options.why: Consistent: every sheet opens the same way regardless of an ask's state.

decision.because: Deliverable 1 says explicitly an ask without a conclusion "keeps its summary as the title, unchanged" — showing summary twice for those 29 asks is not what "unchanged" asked for.

assign.outcome:
**An ask's `conclusion` now leads.** Once the mastermind has weighed an ask and written down its answer, that one plain sentence becomes the card's title — the question that prompted it (`summary`) moves one click down into the sheet, under a small "you asked" label, right above the verbatim quote. An ask with nothing concluded on it yet renders exactly as it always did: id-derived title, summary right on the card. An optional `minutes` shows as a quiet `~N min` beside the status chip only on the rare card that will take the owner longer than a glance — most cards say nothing there. The wall's own head now reads "conclusions first" beside its counts.

Clicking a conclusion-titled card opens the sheet with "you asked" and the right sentence. report-order's band/fold/rank machinery and reply-in-place's reply/mic buttons and dictate box all still render and work — checked in the same run, not assumed.
